correctness.rationale: An induction on source-word length proves the DP by partitioning increasing position subsets according to whether the final position is selected. Exact exhaustive enumeration checks all 32764 nonempty binary inputs of lengths 2..14 and identifies precisely the four length-14 exceptions. The two representatives have unique global maximizers (144 and 147) at length eight, versus 136 and 144 at lengths ≤7. Separate direct 2^14-mask enumeration agrees with every DP-computed subsequence count for each representative; complementation/reversal preservation of counts is a bijection.

value.rationale: The revised universal half-length conjecture is explicitly motivated as enabling a factor-two pattern-length search reduction. A smallest-alphabet binary counterexample, combined with the exact smallest length and complete four-word boundary class, answers the published mathematical question negatively and delineates the first failure. The count 144 versus 136 demonstrates a genuine algorithmic pruning obstruction, not a trivial change of notation or random slice.
